# Gas Turbines
The gas turbine turns hot gas into electrical power. It is the cheap half of the ship's engine room: it needs no fuel mix of its own, only a hot gas feed from something else — a burn chamber, a fusion reactor's waste line, or any other hot loop.
There are two sizes. The **small turbine** is a 3x2 machine for tight engine rooms; the **large turbine** is a 3x5 machine with more than twice the throughput.
## Research and building
- **Small turbine:** research **Atmospherics** and print the small flatpack from an **engineering techfab**. Cargo sells it under Engineering for **1,500 credits**. - **Large turbine:** research **Advanced Atmospherics** and print the large flatpack from an **engineering techfab**. Cargo sells it under Engineering for **5,000 credits**.
The large flatpack costs four times the materials of the small one. Both are printed from steel, glass, plasteel and gold.
## Placing one safely
Turbines are multi-tile machines: the small one covers **3x2 tiles** and the large one **3x5 tiles**, counted from the tile the flatpack sits on. The flatpack refuses to unpack if any of those tiles has no floor, or if a wall, machine, crate, atmos device or **primary-layer pipe** is in the way. Cables and pipes on lower layers are fine — they keep working under the machine.
Stand near the flatpack with a **multitool** in hand and hover the flatpack: a green ghost means the footprint fits, red means something is in the way. Rotate the flatpack with **R** to turn the ghost, then use the multitool on the flatpack. Unpacking takes a few seconds, and the turbine anchors itself when it unfolds.
## Piping and wiring
The turbine creates two pipe stubs when it is anchored: an **inlet** on its west side and an **outlet** on its east side. Pipe your hot gas into the inlet and run the outlet to a waste line or space. Connect the turbine's HV output to the ship's power net.
## Operating
1. Open the turbine UI. It requires **Engineering access**. 2. Set the **flow rate**: how much gas the turbine pulls per second. 3. Set the **stator load**: higher load extracts more power but drags the RPM down. 4. Watch the **RPM** and the temperature. The turbine has a best RPM; overspeeding it and running it too hot both damage the blades.
The turbine reports **overspeed**, **overtemperature**, **stalling** and **undertemperature** states in its UI. A damaged blade set still turns, but it loses efficiency and eventually fails.
## Repair
Weld the turbine with a welding tool to repair blade damage. Each repair costs welding fuel and time; the repair dialogue and the blade health are shown in the UI.
## Tips
- The turbine is most efficient with a steady, hot gas supply. A reactor's waste line is a good match: the turbine turns the leftover heat into power instead of venting it. - Do not feed it cold gas — it will stall. - The stator load can be automated with the two signal ports (increase/decrease).
